Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

critical adjective

finding fault, hard to please

also critical of, fault-finding, hard to please, picky

classical

Cic. Or. 104 (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Sen. 65: mōrōsī et anxiī et īrācundī et difficilēs senēs

mōrōsus, mōrōsa, mōrōsum

adjective, declension

hard to please, captious, fussy

From mōs: someone with his own ways, never satisfied; also peevish, morose (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • difficilis, difficile — hard to please, awkward

    adjective, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Or. 104 (Lewis & Short, s.v. mōrōsus); Traupman 153; Traupman 325

    Of persons, hard to deal with or to satisfy; its everyday sense is “difficult”.

  • criticus, critica, criticum — decisive (of a fever); as a noun, a literary critic

    adjective, declension · avoid · late Latin · Aug. Conf. 6.1 (Lewis & Short); criticus m., a critic: Cic. Fam. 9.10.1; Hor. Ep. 2.1.51

    As an adjective only a doctors’ term, “decisive”, in late Latin; as a noun, a scholar who judges texts and poets. It never means fault-finding.

Examples

  • ūsque eō difficilēs ac mōrōsī sumus, ut nōbīs nōn satisfaciat ipse Dēmosthenēs

    we are so hard to please and so critical that even Demosthenes does not satisfy usCic. Or. 104 (Lewis & Short)

  • Nōlī tam mōrōsus esse; bene cantāvit.

    Don’t be so critical; she sang well.composed

See also crucial.

SourcesLewis & Short: morosus · Lewis & Short: difficilis · Lewis & Short: criticus

Cicero quoted as Lewis & Short quotes him.

The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
